title: Trust Framework
content:
- ### Definition
  - Conceptual and operational model defining trust relationships, trust assumptions, and mechanisms for establishing confidence in narrative system participants. Encompasses identity models, credential systems, and evaluation criteria for assessing trustworthiness.

- ### Semantic Classification
  - owl-class:: infrastructure:TrustFramework
  - owl-role:: Object
  - belongs-to-domain:: [[Narrative Gold Mine]]

- ### Relationships
  - is-subclass-of:: [[Framework]]
  - has-part:: [[Identity Model]], [[Credential System]], [[Trust Evaluation]], [[Trust Assumptions]], [[Revocation Mechanism]]
  - enables:: [[Trust Assessment]], [[Credential Verification]], [[Risk Management]], [[Trustworthiness Assurance]]
  - bridges-to:: [[Trust Infrastructure]], [[Policy Enforcement]] (domain: ngm)
  - depends-on:: [[Trust Infrastructure]]

- ### Content
  The Trust Framework establishes the conceptual model and operational procedures for trust in narrative systems. It defines what credentials are acceptable, how trust is evaluated, and what assumptions are safe to make about participant behaviour. Explicit trust frameworks prevent ambiguity and enable consistent security decision-making.
